rv.q: With a top-notch cast and slick production design, Churchill’s clever concoction of speculative fiction, corporate satire and family drama remains sharp and timely.

Director Lucky Stiff does a fine job shepherding strong performances from the entire cast, but the masterstroke is simply leaving the script alone: putting a 1982 play before a 2026 audience and trusting them to connect the dots themselves—waiting for the moment when the penny drops and the jokes begin to catch in their throats.
Packed with intriguing questions and stellar performances, Top Girls is a must-see.
Lucky Stiff has made this 44-year-old play feel particularly fresh, funny and fashionably new.
The current production at Raven Theatre will leave its mark on you.
Lucky Stiff’s smooth handling of a fine cast for Raven’s mainstage makes it clear why the play deserves its status as a feminist classic.
Lucky Stiff’s direction of this piece is spot on as well, giving each character a moment of greatness amidst the chaos.

Collin Quinn Rice shows up for all three of their roles (waitress at the dinner party, Angie's friend, Kit, and Shona, an interviewee at the Top Girls agency) with a bold commitment to their diverse characters.
Raven Theatre’s production underscores how rigid societal expectations harm not only women but also the LGBTQIA+ community, shaping how individuals view themselves and their worth.
Despite the fascinating questions being raised, the story is much too choppy and overly wordy.

cn.t: Churchill's 1982 feminist classic proves strikingly relevant in Raven Theatre's well-acted production, though its complex exploration of women's ambition and sacrifice in a patriarchal world remains as thorny as ever.
